quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Do not park on the right side of the street.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash through it means you cannot do that action. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look at the right edge of the road. Do not look directly at the bright lights, as this can temporarily blind you.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What is the 'No zone'?

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.
The television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on each side, in the rear, and in the front. Your car cannot be seen in these areas. These are called the 'No zone.'

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the correct lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your signal and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes and put your car in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the right lane to turn, go to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: What type of signs are orange?
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are usually diamond-shaped, orange, and have black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that people are working on or near the highway.

questions.question: What are highway signs that provide information about hazards called?
questions.explanation: Warning signs tell drivers about dangerous conditions ahead. Always obey warning signs to stay safe. Ignoring them can cause accidents.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes wrong.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, changes how you judge speed and distance, makes headlight glare harder to recover from, and often makes you take more risks.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is approaching you on a one-way street. What must you do?

options.text: Move to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights or a siren approaches on a one-way street, move toward the nearest side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for one hour or more.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. The rain brings oil from the asphalt to the road surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat causes more oil to rise.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These conditions make roads slippery. Safety may require you to drive slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: Fog reduces visibility. What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Drive carefully and reduce your speed.
Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.

questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, drive carefully at a slower speed. Do not use high beams. Low beams work better in foggy conditions.

questions.question: When you make a right turn on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You may turn right or left at a green light unless a sign says not to. When you turn, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. What happens?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
The vehicle on the right must let the vehicle on the left go first.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
questions.explanation: Vehicles at a four-way stop usually go in the order they arrive. When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop if other cars are coming.
Come to a complete stop. Go when it is safe.
Go carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only if traffic is on the crossing road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop. Go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop and let vehicles and pedestrians in or entering the intersection go first. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance behind another vehicle?

options.text: When behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting a highway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: When can you continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: What do fluorescent pink signs mean?
questions.explanation: Fluorescent pink signs mark temporary problems on the road. They might indicate a crash or road closure. You should drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: You should signal early before you pass. This gives other drivers time to know your plans.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
You are entering a slower speed zone.
The slower speed zone is over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The slower speed zone is over.
questions.explanation: An "End school zone" sign marks where the slower speed limit ends. You can now drive at the normal speed limit.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass if you are at the top of a hill.
You can pass during the day only.

questions.explanation: Two solid yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving toward you. Never cross these lines to pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Turn on your flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake hard. Grip the steering wheel tightly to stay in your lane. Slow down by releasing the gas pedal. Once you are going very slowly, apply the brakes gently and pull to a safe area.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong coffee to stay awake.
They may drive as poorly as a drunk driver.
Opening a window and turning up the radio is enough to stay alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may drive as poorly as a drunk driver.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive very poorly, just like drunk drivers. Coffee, open windows, and loud radio are not enough to make a drowsy driver safe.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign do?

options.text: Alerts drivers to food and gas locations.

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you of dangers on the road. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if it is open.
If no right lane is open, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear to let them pass.

questions.explanation: Move right if you can. If not, slow down gradually when the road is clear so the tailgater can pass. Never brake hard, as this could cause a crash.

questions.question: Which statements about emergency vehicles are true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens and flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.

questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles pass. They have the right-of-way when using sirens or flashing lights. Follow any loudspeaker instructions. Emergency vehicles may follow each other, so only move when you are sure the way is clear.

questions.question: How can you drive safely at night?

options.text: Do not drive if you are tired.

questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see as well. Take steps to keep yourself and other drivers safe.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you're passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and give them plenty of space. Bicycles offer less protection than cars. Passing too quickly can cause the bicyclist to lose control.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
Turn them slightly to the right.
Turn them sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail. On streets without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: When is it safe to pass on a two-lane, two-way street?

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming cars.
Your car can go fast enough to pass safely.

questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-lane street if you can see the road ahead, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you, and your car is fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.explanation: Stop signs are octagonal (eight-sided). Only stop signs have this shape. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to stop completely before going.

questions.question: What does the "I" stand for in the SIPDE system?
questions.explanation: The "I" in SIPDE means "Identify hazards." Look for road signs, features, and anything that could cause problems.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral and press the brake steadily. Once safe, pull over and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that a red light is coming soon. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through carefully.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement mean?

options.text: You may make the movement if you choose to.
You must make the movement only if traffic lights aren't working.
You must always stop completely before making the movement.
You must make the movement shown while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must make the movement shown while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the pavement tells drivers in that lane which way they must go. Follow traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how well you can stop. Slow down when roads are wet, icy, or in poor condition. Driving too fast on slippery roads makes it hard to stop and control your car.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Dashed white lines can be crossed to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.
